propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing in claim.py and transition.py must be refactored onto stdlib argparse while preserving all existing observable behavior and exit codes

The --force flag has command-specific semantics: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token else defaults to '(no reason given)', while transition bare --force sets force_reason='' without consuming following tokens
The --assignee flag must preserve None-vs-empty-string sentinel behavior: absent invokes default_assignee fallback, explicit empty string clears assignee, value-less raises exit 1

transition._parse_flags must be retained as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) for three external direct callers in test suites

Unknown/extra CLI tokens must be silently skipped via parse_known_args; retired --force-close flag must be explicitly rejected with exit 1 and guidance message; prefix abbreviations must be disabled (allow_abbrev=False)
Help output remains dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help/claim.txt and help/transition.txt (--help out of scope); argparse parser does not generate help
